newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Sarajevans want comeback by multi-ethnic band.
newsitem.headline: Sarajevans want comeback by multi-ethnic band.

text.p: A radio poll on Wednesday showed Sarajevans long for a comeback concert by a legendary Yugoslav rock band whose history strangely mirrors the fate of the war-shattered capital and its citizens.

Bijelo Dugme (White Button), a Sarajevo band that was perhaps the biggest to emerge in old federal Yugoslavia, called it a day in 1989, three years before war engulfed Sarajevo, home of all the band members, and the rest of Bosnia.
The war was prompted by Bosnia's secession from Yugoslavia, echoing breakaways by Croatia and Slovenia, and Sarajevo was devastated by nationalist Serb guns during a 43-month siege.

Independent ISV radio carried out a telephone poll on Wednesday following rumours that the band might regroup for a concert in Croatia's capital Zagreb and found that 99 percent felt it should perform first in Sarajevo.
The band's retirement, as if signalling the end of an era, left a void that other groups could not fill and the siege almost destroyed Sarajevo's rock scene.

The almost unanimous vote is surprising in light of the fact that leader Goran Bregovic, a Serb, declared himself a supporter of the Serbian cause against Bosnian independence and settled in France, ignoring the ordeal of his home town.
Of the three singers Bijelo Dugme had during its 15-year career, one was a Croat, one Moslem and one Serb, reflecting the multi-ethnic composition of Sarajevo and old Yugoslavia.
One band member stayed on in wartime Sarajevo but the others scattered, like many of their fellow citizens.
One of the singers lives in neighbouring Croatia, a drummer went to the United States and another band member committed suicide in the Serbian capital Belgrade last year.
